correction_of_previous_framing.important_boundary: The absence of melt at Giza cannot by itself prove a failed machine, missing phallus/key, or wrong coordinate.

physics_gate.problem: A terrestrial melt-site latitude/longitude cannot be directly overlaid on a fixed RA/Dec because Earth rotates. Without an event epoch/time, local longitude does not determine celestial right ascension.
physics_gate.time_independent_necessary_test: If an incoming local trajectory is independently reconstructed by azimuth A, elevation h, at geographic latitude phi, its celestial declination obeys sin(delta)=sin(phi)sin(h)+cos(phi)cos(h)cos(A). This supplies a necessary 1-D endpoint gate even when RA is unknown.
physics_gate.full_vector_requirement: Exact event time or an independently recovered celestial trajectory is required to reconstruct RA and perform a true 2-D LOVE/EDEM match.
physics_gate.relay_note: For the project route EDEM -> LOVE -> Earth, an actual final incoming ray at Earth would normally arrive from the LOVE direction; testing EDEM as the incident endpoint is retained as a competing model, not silently merged with LOVE.
physics_gate.great_circle_warning: Testing only membership in the EDEM-LOVE great-circle with unknown RA is too permissive to be evidential; endpoint tests are stronger.

site_results.site: Dakhleh Glass, Dakhleh Oasis, Western Desert, Egypt
site_results.why_priority: This was absent from the prior Janus vitrification set and is one of the strongest missed Egyptian physical controls. Its broad glass distribution may permit a future spatial-gradient/airburst trajectory reconstruction.

site_results.site: Libyan Desert Glass field, Great Sand Sea, Egypt
site_results.orion_control: The present Orion Belt population is much younger than the glass event, so the current Belt cannot be its literal source.
site_results.note: Later Egyptian use of LDG is cultural reuse, not evidence that its 28.5 Ma formation was an Osirian event.

site_results.reason: Published trajectory-angle reconstructions differ and event time/RA are not known; matching only declination under one shallow model is not evidence.

site_results.trajectory_model: from east, approximately 30-45 deg above horizontal
site_results.age_note: Published age estimates have changed substantially across studies; no chronology claim is made here from the older registry value.
